s: Which of the following Chandela Kings was not defeated by Mahmud Ghaznavi –

s: Who among the following was the founder of Ghaznavid dynasty?

Sabuktigin (977-997) founded the Ghaznavid dynasty; Alptigin had only seized Ghazni (962) as a Samanid general, and Mahmud was Sabuktigin's son (some guide-book keys: Alptigin).

s: What was the main motive of Mahmud Ghaznavi in context of invasion of India?
o: To make the country its colony.
x: Mahmud raided mainly to plunder temple wealth; he never tried to annex India beyond Punjab.

s: Who fought the Battle of Waihind (AD 1009)?
x: At Waihind (1008-09), near Peshawar, the Hindu Shahi Anandapala was defeated by Mahmud of Ghazni.

s: Of what nationality was Ibn Battuta, who visited India during the reign of Muhammad-Bin- Tughlaq? as by A)
x: Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan from Tangiers who came to India under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

s: "The king was freed from his people and they from their king". On whose death did Badauni comment thus? Medieval Indian History PMF IAS IH – 38
x: Badauni wrote this on the death of Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1351), not Balban, Alauddin or Firoz.

s: On the death of which Muslim ruler, a historian said ‘the king was freed from his people and they from their king’?
x: The remark is Badauni's on the death of Muhammad bin Tughlaq near Thatta in 1351.

s: Ibn Batuta’s work, Rihla, completed in 1355, is
o: an account of the Delhi Sultans from Aibek to Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.
an account of trade with Morocco.
x: The CDS 2013 key is "an account of the Delhi Sultans from Aibak to Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq": the India part of the Rihla retells Sultanate history before Ibn Battuta's own time. It is a travelogue, not a religious text or an account of Moroccan trade.

s: Ibn Battuta, the Moorish traveller, visited India during the reign of :
x: The Moorish (Moroccan) Ibn Battuta came in 1333 under Muhammad bin Tughlaq, who made him Qazi of Delhi.

s: Who among the following appointed Ibn Battuta as the Chief Qazi of Delhi?
x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq made Ibn Battuta Qazi of Delhi and in 1342 sent him to China as envoy.

s: Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of :
x: Ibn Battuta reached India in 1333, in Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign (1325-51) – not Firoz's, Ghiyasuddin's or Bahlul's.

s: During Sultanate period, 'Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi' was related with which of the following?
x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was MBT's department of agriculture, to bring waste land under cultivation – not the army, revenue or entertainment.

s: Who amongst the following established ‘Diwan-e-amirkothi’ during Delhi Sultanate?
x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was set up by Muhammad bin Tughlaq – not Alauddin, Firoz or Iltutmish.

s: Which Sultan of Delhi had established a separate Agriculture Department and had planned the ‘rotation of crops’ ?
x: MBT created the separate agriculture department (Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi), which planned better crops and crop rotation in a trial block; Iltutmish, Balban and Alauddin are not linked with it.

s: Which ruler established 'Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi' department?
x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was Muhammad bin Tughlaq's agriculture department, not Firoz's or Alauddin's.

s: Diwan-E-Kohi is associated with–
x: Diwan-i-Kohi (Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi) was the agriculture department of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

s: With reference to medieval Indian rulers, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Alauddin Khalji first set up a separate Ariz's department
Balban introduced the branding system of horses of military
Muhammad bin Tughlaq was succeeded by his uncle to the Delhi throne
Firuz Tughlaq set up a separate department of slaves
x: Firoz set up the Diwan-i-Bandagan, a separate department of slaves. Horse branding was Alauddin's, the Ariz department Balban's, and MBT was succeeded by his cousin Firoz, not an uncle.

s: With reference to medieval Indian rulers, which one of the following statement is correct?
o: Alauddin Khilji first set up a separate Ariz’s department.
Balban introduced the branding system of horses for his military.
Muhammad-bin-Tughluq was succeeded by his uncle to the throne.
Firuz Shah Tughlaq set up a separate department of slaves.
x: Firoz set up the Diwan-i-Bandagan for slaves. Dagh was Alauddin's, the Ariz department Balban's, and Firoz was MBT's cousin.

s: Ain-ul-Mulk Multani did not serve under which of the following rulers?
x: Ain-ul-Mulk Multani won Malwa for Alauddin (1305) and later served MBT and Firoz; he lived long after Iltutmish (d. 1236).

s: Which Sultan of Delhi made a rule that, in any given year, the land revenue can be increased only nominally, viz one-tenth or one-eleventh of the fixed revenue?
x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq allowed any increase in land revenue of only about one-tenth (one-eleventh) a year. Alauddin had raised it to half; Balban and Firoz are not linked to this rule.

s: Which technique was used in times of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq for measurement of Khalisa land?
x:
Printed key: Kankut. Moreland and IGNOU: Ghiyasuddin replaced measurement by crop-sharing (batai); galla-bakhshi is another name for sharing, so batai is keyed.
Ghiyasuddin dropped Alauddin's measurement (masahat) and assessed khalisa land by sharing the actual crop (batai / hukm-i-hasil). The printed key Kankut is wrong: kankut is estimation of the standing crop, not sharing.

s: The Hindu king that has given shelter to Bahauddin Gurshasp who revolted against Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq in A.D.1326.
x: Bahauddin Gurshasp, MBT's cousin, revolted in 1326 and fled to Kampila Deva of Kampili; MBT then took Kampili and captured Harihara and Bukka. The Reddi and Musunuri chiefs rose only later.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Tughluq dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
x: Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah (1394-1412) was the last Tughlaq; Nusrat Shah was only his rival at Firozabad.
